one_liner: Statically typed, Cranelift-JIT-compiled scripting language for Rust hosts; about 1.3x faster than Lua 5.5 (mlua) on a Rust-object sort benchmark.
what_it_does: Roto is an embedded scripting language for Rust applications, built by NLnet Labs for filters in the Rotonda BGP engine. The host registers Rust types, functions and methods with the library! macro, compiles a .roto file with Runtime::compile, and gets typed function handles (pkg.get_function::<fn(u64) -> u64>("main")) it can call like Rust functions. It is a separate language (Rust-like syntax, type inference, filtermap/accept/reject constructs), not a Lua or JS replacement, so existing scripts do not carry over.
how_it_is_fast: Scripts are type-checked ahead of time and compiled to native machine code with the Cranelift JIT (opt_level "speed"), so there is no bytecode interpreter loop and no dynamic type checks. Registered Rust types are passed by value with no serialization or userdata boxing, and registered Rust functions are called directly from the generated code. Runtime data structures are implemented in Rust: List is a type-erased Arc<Mutex<Vec>>-like shared array (one lock per operation) and String is Arc<str>.
when_to_use: Rust host that needs user-editable filters or policies over its own Rust types (the Rotonda BGP-filter use case: IP addresses, prefixes, routes).

Workloads dominated by calls between script and Rust: the shootout calls a registered Rust comparison inside an in-script quicksort of 10,000 Rust objects and Roto beat mlua Lua 5.5 (12.04 vs 15.47 ms) and rquickjs (36.38 ms).
You want type errors caught when the script is loaded, not at run time, and can accept a statically typed language for scripting.
Hot-reloadable logic where the host recompiles scripts at run time and keeps typed function handles (TypedFunc is Send + Sync).
when_not_to_use: You need existing Lua or JavaScript scripts, a large standard library or an ecosystem: Roto has no generics, no first-class functions and no maps/dictionaries yet (README 'Pending features').

Untrusted scripts in-process: the README says a script can exhaust memory through infinite recursion, loop forever with while, or be large enough to slow compilation; there is no instruction budget, so it recommends a separate process with a timeout.
Peak speed on this kind of workload: in the same chart Luau through mlua with its JIT enabled (11.82 ms), Wasmi (7.04 ms) and Wasmtime (2.71 ms) are faster than Roto.
Non-Rust hosts: the embedding API is Rust-only, and registered types must be Clone (or wrapped in Rc/Arc), PartialEq, Send + Sync and 'static.
You need a stable language: 0.x releases keep breaking syntax and API (0.11 changed comments, match arms, negation and the string type).

integration.dependencies: cranelift, cranelift-codegen, cranelift-jit (0.127 in release 0.12.0, 0.136 on main), ariadne, inetnum, symbol_table, indexmap, sealed, libc, log, unicode-ident, rustc-literal-escaper, roto-macros; clap optional (default 'cli' feature, disable with default-features = false)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 (rust-version of crates.io 0.12.0, edition 2024); main now declares 1.96
integration.platforms: Hosts with a Cranelift native back end (cranelift::native picks the running ISA); benchmark measured on Apple M5 Max (aarch64). Panics on x86_64 were fixed on main after 0.12.0 (Cranelift 0.136 upgrade plus is_pic).
integration.thread_safety: TypedFunc and compiled module data are marked Send + Sync (unsafe impl); registered types must be Send + Sync; Lists lock an internal Mutex on every operation. No other concurrency documentation found.

gotchas: The only cross-engine numbers measure script-to-Rust interop, not interpreter speed. The Roto script was tuned by the Roto maintainer (script-bench-rs PRs #17 and #18 made list swap a native Rust call) while the Lua and JS ports swap in-script; the Roto charset has 15 characters against 16; the JS port builds each string with new Array(len) and then pushes, so it joins a 2*len holey array; the Lua 5.5 run replaces table.create with a Rust callback. Each run is validated as sorted with 10,000 elements, so no no-op timing was found.

Lists are shared by reference (Arc<Mutex>): passing a list to a function mutates the caller's list, and every get, push or swap takes a mutex lock (Roto's own insertion_sort bench notes that cloning a List does not copy it).
Release 0.12.0 on crates.io still uses Cranelift 0.127; the fix for panics on x86_64 (#461, merged 2026-09-22) is only on main, so x86_64 users should test or build from main.

Roto relies on unsafe code to call generated machine code; the README treats any unsoundness as a high-priority bug and runs tests under Valgrind in CI, but a JIT bug is a memory-safety bug in the host. The 0.12 changelog lists miscompilation fixes (#446).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Roto over Luau (faster in the same chart, 11.82 ms) or Lua 5.5 via mlua when the host is Rust and you want typed scripts that work on registered Rust types directly with no userdata glue. Pick Luau or Lua when you need a mature dynamic language with sandboxing and existing scripts. Lua-CSharp and the other siblings target other hosts (.NET, C, Go).
verified_claims_summary: In khvzak/script-bench-rs (mlua author, refreshed 2026-10-03; rustc 1.99.0, opt-level 3, fat LTO, codegen-units 1, criterion sample size 10, Apple M5 Max, macOS 27.0), Roto 0.12.0 took 12.04 ms to build 10,000 random strings as Rust objects and quicksort them with a Rust comparison, against 15.47 ms for vendored Lua 5.5 through mlua 0.12.2 and 36.38 ms for QuickJS through rquickjs 0.14.0 (about 1.3x and 3.0x, derived from page data). Roto's README itself makes no speed claim.
